issues.title: feat(tui): motion controls — configurable spinner cadence, frame-rate ceiling, and a motion preset
issues.body:
## What

4fps looks fine - slightly jerky, but when I've got a dozen omp windows open I'd rather have the CPU available for real work. This PR gives users that control over the terminal re-renders omp's animations cause — down to no animation at all — while every default stays exactly where it is for single-pane users.

A working omp session repaints its terminal about 30 times a second and writes its title 12.5 times a second, every second it works. That is fine for one pane. With dozens of panes under tmux control mode every frame is a composite for the host terminal and every title write is relayed to every attached client — profiled on my laptop as the dominant main-thread cost in iTerm2. Until now only the working-row shimmer could be switched off (`display.shimmer`); the spinner cadence, the render scheduler's ceiling, the title spinner, and the status-line blink/fade had no controls.

Three commits, each reviewable alone, every default unchanged:

1. **`tui.spinnerInterval`** (ms, default 80, `0` = static) — one cadence for every spinner: `pi-tui` gains a shared spinner clock (`spinner-clock.ts`: live interval, change listeners, one phase function `sharedSpinnerFrame`, `0` → frame 0 and no spinner timers) that the Loader rows, live tool cards and the status-line brand spinner read; their timers also *fire* on that clock's boundaries (`spinnerTickDelay`), so N spinners on screen wake the renderer once per period and cost one frame — previously each owner ticked from its own start time and two spinners 120 ms apart painted twice per period (8 frames/s at a 250 ms cadence); the terminal-title spinner takes its period from the same setting. `--spinner-interval <ms>`, `PI_SPINNER_INTERVAL`. Replaces the hardcoded `SPINNER_ADVANCE_MS`.
2. **`tui.maxFps`** (default 30, 1–120) — the render scheduler's cadence floor becomes `1000 / maxFps` (`frame-rate.ts`). It works upward too, for those so inclined: `tui.maxFps: 60` in `config.yml` (or `--max-fps 60`, `PI_MAX_FPS=60`) lifts the old fixed 30 fps floor for content and keystroke frames — the range is 1–120, and the only other limiter is the existing adaptive backpressure (next frame no sooner than 2× the last frame's cost), so a fast terminal with cheap frames gets 60+; measured ~50–56 frames/s here on a fast stream. Animations keep their own cadences (shimmer 30 Hz, spinners at `tui.spinnerInterval`). Keystroke echo is exempt: every terminal input sets a latch in `#handleInput` (before any consumer runs), and a render requested while it is set — by the focused component or by an input listener (scroll wheel, toggles) — rides at least the 30 fps input cadence (the ceiling itself when that is faster), replacing an animation frame parked further out; input that triggers no render leaves the latch for the next frame to consume once. The adaptive-backpressure floor, the Esc/Ctrl-C grace, the output-backlog deferral and the native (TSP) path are unchanged. Animation timers (Loader, shared tool ticker) never tick faster than a frame can land, so CPU drops with the paints. `--max-fps <n>`, `PI_MAX_FPS`.
3. **`tui.motion`** = `full` | `reduced` | `none` (default `full` = today) — one switch over the animations: `reduced` = spinners at 250 ms, shimmer off, no blink/fade; `none` = static spinners and title, shimmer off, no blink/fade. Decorative motion with no knob of its own — the status-line speculation blink and brand fade, and the editor's magic-keyword shimmer — is switched off with it on both the ANSI and the native (TSP `quietMotion`) paths, so `none` really means no animation anywhere; a magic keyword stays highlighted, it just stops sweeping. Neither preset lowers `tui.maxFps`: the animations pace themselves, so a lower ceiling would only throttle content — streaming text keeps repainting at full rate under both presets, and an explicit `tui.maxFps` / `--max-fps` remains the way to throttle a pane wholesale. (An earlier revision had the presets set a 4 fps ceiling; in a deployed build that made streaming text visibly choppy, which is the opposite of the intent.) The preset→values mapping is one dependency-free module; a single `Derived` resolves the effective settings, and a `tui.spinnerInterval`, `tui.maxFps` or `display.shimmer` the user set explicitly wins over the preset at read time (the preset never writes them). The status-line speculation blink and brand fade get a decorative-motion switch the preset drives. `--motion <mode>`, `PI_MOTION`; `display.shimmer` also gains `--shimmer <mode>` and `PI_SHIMMER`.

Precedence for every knob follows the registry: env > flag > setting (documented as such).

## Why

The spinner's cost is paid by the terminal, not by omp, and it scales with pane count and attached clients; the title cost scales with *all* panes (tmux forwards OSC titles from background windows), the render cost with visible ones. The defaults were tuned for a single foreground pane and stay that way; this adds the controls to go quieter, and one preset so the many-pane case is one flag or one environment variable.

## Testing

- `bun check` on the pushed SHA (4769a137ed): the TypeScript half (`check:tools` + every package's `check:types`) is clean. The Rust half is not verifiable on this machine — `check:rs` needs the pinned `nightly-2026-08-12` rustfmt (no rustup here) and the stable rustfmt 1.9.0 reports the same 2991 formatting diffs on pristine `main`; this PR touches no Rust files. Left unticked for CI to confirm.
- `bun check` clean (`check:types` for coding-agent and tui, root `check:tools`).
- Contract tests, each failing without its change: a working row and a live tool card started out of phase paint once per period through the real TUI (16 paints in 4 s at 250 ms, was 32) and show the same glyph; the editor's magic-keyword shimmer arms a sweep with motion on, none with it off (keyword still highlighted), and a live switch off cancels a pending frame; spinner cadence transitions (slow / static pins frame 0 and stops timers / re-arm) for the Loader and the shared tool ticker; scheduler pacing with a fake `RenderScheduler` (animation frame at the ceiling; keystroke within one 30 fps frame at a 1 fps ceiling; keystroke replaces a parked animation timer; input renders still obey the adaptive floor; a backlog-deferred keystroke frame keeps its priority; a consumed key and a wheel sequence from an input listener are paced at the input cadence); preset precedence (`none` + explicit 80 ms → spinners animate while the ceiling applies), the settings derivation live and from disk, flag parsing/rejection; brand fade armed by default and absent with effects off. Full `pi-tui` suite: 3260 pass (3 pre-existing environmental failures reproduce on `main`).
- Measured on a PTY with a slow mock provider holding the session in the working state (100×30, 8–10 s window, counting synchronized-output paints and OSC title writes):

  | configuration (one token per 600 ms) | frames/s | title writes/s | bytes/s (approx., ±10% run to run) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | defaults (before and after) | 29.4–29.9 | 12.3–12.5 | ~15 000 |
  | `--spinner-interval 250` | 29.8 | 4.0 | ~8 000 |
  | `--max-fps 4` | 4.0 | 12.4 | ~3 500 |
  | `--motion reduced` | 10.3 | 4.0 | ~3 400 |
  | `--motion none` | 8.9 | 0 | ~3 200 |
  | `--motion none --spinner-interval 80` | 17.5 | 12.4 | ~8 400 |
  | `--motion reduced --max-fps 4` | 4.0 | 4.0 | ~2 500 |

  With a fast stream (one token per 40 ms): defaults 29.9 / 12.4; `--motion reduced` 29.8 / 4.0; `--motion none` 29.9 / 0 — text streams at the full 30 fps while the title and spinners stay quiet. Under the presets the remaining frames are the content itself (each token repaints the message, the rate meter and the token counters) plus the one-second elapsed timers; with no tokens arriving, `none` idles at ~2 frames/s (the two elapsed timers tick out of phase).

  The `--spinner-interval 80` and `--max-fps 4` rows are the precedence rule end to end: an explicit knob wins over the preset for that knob while the rest of the preset still applies. Harness: a Bun script that serves a mock `openai-completions` provider streaming one token every 600 ms, launches `bun src/cli.ts --no-extensions --no-session --model mock/mock-slow [flags] "stream a long answer please"` on a fresh PTY under an isolated `HOME`, and counts `ESC[?2026h` paints and `ESC]0;` title writes per second over the window — `CAPTURE_S=8 bun measure.ts <checkout> --motion none` and so on. Not part of the repo (a bench, not a test); happy to attach it on request.
- Exercised locally in iTerm2 + tmux control mode with several omp panes at `--motion reduced` and `none`; typing in the focused pane echoes at full rate at every ceiling.
- Terminal-side cost, measured on the deployed build (iTerm2 under tmux control mode, a dozen managed omp panes launched with `--motion reduced`, 30 s `top` averages of the iTerm2 process on a 14-core Mac): a waiting pane's spinner costs iTerm2 ~0.3–0.6% of a core; a streaming pane ~10–20%, and only while it streams. Before this change the terminal sat around 50% regardless of what the panes were doing — spinner and title churn across every pane — so CPU now goes only to panes painting new content.

Supersedes #14201 (a title-only interval knob): its validator fix and review redress are carried in commit 1.

---

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] CHANGELOG updated with the required attribution (if user-facing; internal issue fixes use issue links, external contributions add the PR link and contributor credit after creation)

issues.title: fix(tui): retain wait snapshots beside turn usage
issues.body:
## What

Keep still-running wait snapshots visible after they are sealed, and retain the snapshot beside a completed turn's usage row when another wait starts. The legacy and native renderers both preserve running jobs; the transcript container prevents discarding the content immediately above a usage row.

## Why

Fixes #12248. A nonempty wait result could become a blank historical card, or its card could be displaced while its token/cost row remained. Sealing now freezes the waiting snapshot rather than erasing it. Consecutive polls without an intervening usage row still coalesce. Token totals, accounting, wait cadence, and process timeouts are unchanged.

## Testing

- Reproduced on upstream `cccb74456fb6a0f0e161de8f4b7cba23ac148822` with the repository's real `ToolExecutionComponent` and EventController harness: sealing an all-running wait rendered an empty result, and the next wait removed the prior card while its usage remained. Both regressions failed before the production fix and pass afterward.
- Repository regressions also exercise both `UiHelpers` session replay and `ChatTranscriptBuilder` replay: two completed wait turns retain their worker snapshots immediately above their original 4.2K and 2.1K input-token rows, without duplicating metrics. Existing same-turn wait/todo displacement remains covered.
- Sealed mixed-job, all-running and native wait-card coverage passes.
- Final focused run: `bun test --timeout 30000` over wait-render, transcript-container, job-poll-displacement and usage-row-placement: 73 passed / 238 assertions. The existing deep-link test exceeds the default 5-second timeout on both unmodified upstream and this branch; it passed in 8.95 seconds with the longer timeout.
- `bun check` ran: lint/format and other package typechecks passed, but the new native renderer test initially used the wrong argument count. After correcting that test-only call, the affected TUI package's full lint/format/typecheck passed. The full root command was not rerun after that correction, so its checklist remains unchecked. `git diff --check` passed.
- This uses deterministic repository UI harnesses without model/provider inference. Live model-backed interactive operation and contributor personal review are not claimed.

---

- [ ] `bun check` passes
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] CHANGELOG updated with the required attribution (if user-facing; internal issue fixes use issue links, external contributions add the PR link and contributor credit after creation)

issues.title: feat(ui): add reduce-motion setting to freeze terminal animations
issues.body:
## What

Adds a `display.reduceMotion` setting (`off` | `on` | `strict`, default `off`) and a matching `--reduce-motion` launch flag that freezes cosmetic terminal animations:

- `on` freezes theme-driven spinners (via a single-frame freeze at the `Theme.getSpinnerFrames` choke point, covering every `theme.spinnerFrames` / `getSymbolTheme().spinnerFrames` consumer), disables shimmer and smooth streaming, and stops the terminal-title spinner, welcome intro, startup splash, codex fireworks, live-mic hue rotation, and todo-strike sweep.
- `strict` additionally caps TUI repaint rate at ~4fps via `TUI.setMinRenderInterval(250)`.
- `--reduce-motion` (with optional `on`/`strict`/`off` value) is a session-only override; the setting is live-reapplied when changed in `/config`.

Central helper: `src/config/reduce-motion.ts` (`isReduceMotion()`, `reduceMotionLevel()`). The freeze point is memoized per source-array identity, so it costs nothing when reduce-motion is off.

## Why

Accessibility (photosensitive users, vestibular motion sensitivity) and low-bandwidth/remote sessions where continuous repaint churn is wasteful. This was previously only partially possible via `display.shimmer: disabled`, which does not freeze spinners or title animation.

## Testing

- `bun check` passes in `packages/coding-agent` (biome + tsgo) and `packages/tui`.
- `bun test` green: `test/cli-reduce-motion-flag.test.ts`, `test/title-generator.test.ts`, `test/startup-splash.test.ts` (48 tests), `test/tools/todo.test.ts` (73 tests), and `packages/tui/test/loader.test.ts` (14 tests).
- Smoke-tested interactively in a PTY: spinners freeze to a single frame under `on`; `strict` caps repaint cadence.

---

- [x] `bun check` passes
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing)
issues.display_title: feat(ui): add reduce-motion setting to freeze terminal animations

issues.title: feat(theme): add assistantMessageText token for assistant prose
issues.body:
## Problem

Assistant paragraph prose had no theme token and always rendered at the terminal default foreground, so a theme could not distinguish assistant prose from other text ([#11204](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/11204)).

## Change

- Adds an **optional** `assistantMessageText` theme token (`colors.assistantMessageText`), wired through the ArkType theme schema, `theme-schema.json`, the `ThemeColor` union, and `THEME_COLOR_RECORD`.
- The assistant message component paints its markdown prose with the token when the theme declares one and keeps the terminal default when it does not; an explicitly installed prose color transform still wins.
- Optional tokens now resolve to the terminal default inside `Theme` when a theme omits them (`OPTIONAL_THEME_COLOR_RECORD`). Without that, a theme color list entry naming an optional token — e.g. a `modelTags.<role>.color` reference, which is validated against the theme color list — would make `theme.fg()` throw `Unknown theme color` for every built-in theme, none of which declare this token.

## Verification

- `bun test test/modes/components/assistant-message-prose-color.test.ts` → 4 pass / 0 fail. Covers: prose painted with the token, prose left at the terminal default when the token is unset, an injected prose transform overriding the token, and an omitted optional token resolving to the terminal default instead of throwing.
- The escapes are derived from the theme's own public accessor rather than hard-coded, so the suite passes in both color depths (verified: `env -u WT_SESSION -u COLORTERM -u TERM_PROGRAM bun test …` for 256color and the default truecolor path). A literal truecolor SGR previously passed locally (Windows Terminal sets `WT_SESSION`) and failed on CI.
- Pre-fix control: with the source reverted, the token test fails in both modes; with the optional-token fallback removed, the new fallback test fails with `Unknown theme color: assistantMessageText`.
- Adjacent theme/UI suites (theme components, settings-list theme, shimmer, epoch fallback, export-html themes) → 35 pass / 0 fail; `bun check:types` clean; `bunx oxfmt --check` clean on every changed TS file.
issues.display_title: feat(theme): add assistantMessageText token for assistant prose
